lede: Higher β blurs the digit, and diversity peaks at β = 1 rather than at the search pick.
title: β-VAE on digits
question: What does the KL weight do to reconstruction, active latent axes, and sample diversity?
process: The loss is the same one used for the comparison VAE. The only new coefficient is β, and it multiplies the KL term rather than the pixels:

A traversal does not retrain the model. It starts at the zero code and moves one coordinate from −3 to 3 while the decoder draws the image. An axis counts as active when its posterior mean still varies across the test set, with variance above 0.01.

With every other setting held fixed, Optuna scored β = 0.1, 1, 4, and 10 at validation losses 100.4, 117.8, 152.0, and 189.5. A 10-epoch sweep puts the diversity peak at β = 1 (0.226) and the sharpest test MSE at β = 0.1 (0.091).

opening.summary: Optuna picks β = 0.1 on the weighted loss. Diversity peaks at β = 1. Each value of β has its own traversal.
opening.hover: Each point is one value of β.

charts.title: Test error, active axes, and diversity

marks.summary: β = 0.1 has the sharpest reconstructions in the sweep, with test MSE 0.0907, and all 8 axes stay active. Per-axis KL sits in a narrow band, about 3.1 to 3.8. Every traversal row changes the digit. Diversity is 0.168, tighter than at β = 1. Optuna picks this β because it minimizes the weighted loss. That is the best reconstruction here, not the most compact code.
marks.hover: β = 0.1. MSE 0.0907, KL 26.94, 8 active axes, diversity 0.168.
marks.frameCaption: β = 0.1. Every row still changes the digit.

marks.summary: β = 1 is marked on these panels because diversity peaks here, at 0.226. Test MSE rises only to 0.0940, all 8 axes stay active, and the KL falls to 15.03. The traversal rows still change the glyph. Optuna does not pick this point. It picks β = 0.1, where the weighted validation loss is lower and the samples are tighter.
marks.hover: β = 1. MSE 0.0940, KL 15.03, 8 active axes, diversity 0.226.
marks.frameCaption: β = 1. Every row still moves the glyph.

marks.answers: Why do you think the results might not be great?
marks.summary: β = 4 pushes test MSE to 0.1114 and the KL down to 8.37. Active axes fall to 7. One axis, z4, has a KL of about 0.007 and a traversal response near zero. Diversity slips to 0.204. The code is getting smaller by switching an axis off, and the digits are blurrier.
marks.hover: β = 4. MSE 0.1114, KL 8.37, 7 active axes, diversity 0.204.
marks.frameCaption: β = 4. The rows still move, and the digits are blurrier.

marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: β = 10 is the blurriest decoder in the sweep, with test MSE 0.1480, and the least diverse prior, at 0.151. The KL is 3.94. z3, z4, and z5 each have a KL under 0.02, and their traversal rows barely move, so three rows of the grid stay a single glyph. The rows that still move still change which digit you see. That is unused axes turning off, not one axis taking ownership of slant. MNIST does not label a continuous factor, so the grid is not evidence of disentanglement.
marks.hover: β = 10. MSE 0.1480, KL 3.94, 6 active axes, diversity 0.151.
marks.frameCaption: β = 10. Several rows stay one smeared digit.

marks.summary: β = 0.1 is marked because Optuna minimizes the β-weighted validation loss, and this trial scores 100.37. Hidden size, dropout, learning rate, weight decay, batch size, and latent size were the same on every trial, so the comparison isolates β. The saved hyperparameters store this value. It is the best reconstruction weight in the search, and it is the low-diversity end of the sweep.
marks.frameCaption: β = 0.1. Every row still changes the digit.

marks.summary: β = 1 scores a validation loss of 117.77. The weighted objective is worse than at 0.1, and the exploration sweep says this is where diversity peaks. The search and the sample grid want different values of β.
marks.frameCaption: β = 1. Every row still moves the glyph.

marks.answers: Why do you think the results might not be great?
marks.summary: β = 4 scores a validation loss of 151.98. In the longer sweep, test MSE is 0.1114, active axes fall to 7, and one traversal row goes quiet. The objective and the pictures agree that the code is being squeezed.
marks.frameCaption: β = 4. The rows still move, and the digits are blurrier.

marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: β = 10 is the worst Optuna loss, at 189.53, and the blurriest point in the sweep: test MSE 0.1480, diversity 0.151, and six active axes. z3, z4, and z5 have a KL under 0.02, and their traversal rows barely move. The frozen rows are unused axes. MNIST does not label a continuous factor, so the grid is not evidence of disentanglement.
marks.frameCaption: β = 10. Several rows stay one smeared digit.

reflection.worked: Optuna’s lowest weighted loss is β = 0.1, at 100.37, and that point in the sweep has test MSE 0.0907 with all 8 axes active. Diversity peaks at β = 1, at 0.226. The traversal shows which row moves.
reflection.unexpected: The search picks the reconstruction weight, not the diverse one. At β = 10, three traversal rows freeze and only six axes stay active.
reflection.why: β is the multiplier on the KL, and an axis counts as active when the variance of its posterior mean is above 0.01. MNIST has no labeled factor such as slant, so a frozen row is unused capacity rather than a discovered factor. That last point is a reading of the grid, not a disentanglement result.
reflection.improve: Put diversity next to the Optuna loss, or the search will keep choosing a small β. Keep β near 1 when the goal is the sample grid. Use a dataset with known factors if the claim is disentanglement.
